name: Product Boundary and Runtime Topology
purpose: Define the smallest stable Beta 1.0 runtime/process/network boundary so downstream HLD and LLD packets can design implementation details without rediscovering product topology.

decisions.decision: One authoritative Python host process owns each canonical SOMA data instance.
The browser is a same-machine presentation client and is not the application lifetime or domain authority.
Beta 1.0 has no second authoritative worker/service; background work is host-supervised and restart-safe through HLD-02 durable state.
The host serves both the local application API and version-matched browser assets on an exact supported loopback origin.
Closing/restarting the browser does not stop the host; tray and explicit start/stop controls manage host lifetime.
Beta 1.0 runtime operation requires no internet, CDN, cloud service, remote database service, or installed Node.js runtime.

HLD-01 intentionally does not select implementation technologies beyond the Python-host topology. LLD-01 selects the Python server/host integration and loopback-port mechanics; LLD-10 selects the browser client/frontend framework, language and build tool; LLD-12 selects tray/installer/package integration and supported-browser packaging constraints. All remain constrained by offline operation and no installed Node.js runtime requirement.

unresolved_here_by_design: O-006 exact Windows editions/builds, browser versions, runner images, packaging combinations
O-010 exact tray toolkit and low-level background lifecycle implementation
exact Python server framework and loopback port-selection algorithm -> LLD-01
exact tray toolkit, installer technology and browser/package support matrix -> LLD-12
